abstract: As conversational AI tools like ChatGPT become increasingly integrated into education, concerns have emerged about how negative information (linguistic cues emphasizing uncertainty, difficulty, or risk) may influence adolescents’ trust and learning behaviors. This study examined associations between negative ChatGPT responses, adolescents’ AI distrust, and learning-related outcomes, including motivation and discontinuation. Among 250 adolescents aged 12–13 who completed a 10-minute ChatGPT-based learning activity on inductive and deductive reasoning, analyses of 195 participants indicated that greater frequency of and initial exposure to negative information were associated with higher AI distrust, which was related to lower learning motivation and greater learning discontinuation. Moreover, dissatisfaction with ChatGPT’s responses moderated these relationships, such that associations between AI distrust and lower learning motivation and greater learning discontinuation were stronger among more dissatisfied adolescents. These findings underscore the importance of how negative AI-generated information is communicated, given its potential implications for adolescents’ trust, motivation, and continued learning engagement.

ur.tldr: 在195名完成ChatGPT推理学习的12—13岁青少年中，负面信息的出现频率及首次暴露与更高的AI不信任相关；不信任又对应更低学习动机和更多中途放弃。回答不满会强化这种负面影响，凸显AI回应措辞与内容设计的重要性。

title: Why do students discontinue learning with ChatGPT? The role of negative information in reducing motivation and learning discontinuation
title_zh: 学生为何停止使用ChatGPT学习？负面信息对动机降低与学习中止的作用
